question: Can a cross-validation-tuned, class-balanced LightGBM classifier choose a better per-instance local-search parameter setting than a standard MLP configuration predictor on generated knapsack instances, judged by the same held-out solution quality?
method: Generated 0/1 knapsack instances (fixed seed) labelled with the best local-search setting under a fixed evaluation budget; MLP baseline vs CV-tuned class-balanced LightGBM; test set from a shifted instance family; evaluated by mean normalised solution quality.
metric_name: mean normalised solution quality (value / optimum) on held-out test instances
baseline: Standard MLPClassifier (64-32 hidden, scaled features) predicting the local-search setting
improved: Class-balanced LightGBM with 3-fold CV-tuned hyperparameters on the same features and labels
notes: Labels are noisy (single small grid, budget-limited search); test family is shifted in size and correlation, so tree models cannot extrapolate in size. Test set used once for both models; LightGBM tuning used only training CV. Results depend on the generator and budget and are not a replication of OPTICAT's deep RL results.
